name: Nick Fuentes
role: American white-nationalist and Catholic-integralist streamer and commentator (host of America First, b. 1998)
summary: Fuentes advocates an America First nationalism centred on a predominantly white and Christian country, mass deportation, opposition to US support for Israel, and male authority in family and public life. He opposes women’s suffrage and supports a powerful executive; his economic proposals include protective tariffs, strategic industrial subsidies and public works.

abortion-legal.rationale: In the Carlson interview he describes abortion as killing children in the womb and says almost all abortions are elective.

allow-dual-citizenship.rationale: In the Carlson interview he explicitly endorses banning dual citizenship as a measure against conflicting foreign allegiances.

corporate-influence.rationale: Told Piers Morgan to "get the money out of politics, the super PACs, the special interests" and to drain the swamp.

democracy-best.rationale: Asked by Neel whether America should abandon democracy, he agrees and argues for less popular power and checks on voters.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Told Piers Morgan he does not want his white children marrying black people ("It's racial for me") and, challenged on being against interracial marriage, defended the position rather than retracting it.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Told Piers Morgan women should not have equal rights or the vote because the sexes have different roles; told Carlson the husband has final authority and the wife is subordinate.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: In the Carlson interview he describes the country as too diverse and agrees that tribal interests must give way to national interests for it to stay together.

elite-replacement.rationale: In the Morgan interview he attributes open borders and demographic displacement to the deliberate postwar open-society project, rather than merely observing a changing population.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Neel interview explicitly proposes martial law and locking down major cities with National Guard troops to overcome what he calls open rebellion; this goes beyond the earlier evidence about ordinary arrests.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: In the Morgan interview he affirms equality before God but expressly rejects equal legal rights for women; that rejects the equal-rights clause without attributing unequal spiritual worth to him.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Told Piers Morgan that Israel's aim of keeping a Jewish majority is "my politics" and that whites and Christians becoming a minority in America is the problem; told Carlson the demographics must be conserved. He also said "not to the exclusion of everybody else".

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Holds women should not vote and should be treated differently in law, so opposes required parity in public bodies.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Told Piers Morgan the two genders are biologically distinct with different biological and social roles, and told Carlson sex roles are natural.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The Morgan interview contains his earlier denial clips and his later acceptance of six million or more deaths, alongside continued questioning. The contrary words do not establish a sustained replacement of the older position, so the evidence is mixed rather than a newer denial of denial.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: In the Morgan interview he invokes biblical restrictions on women teaching and exercising authority as the justification for different legal treatment of the sexes. This supports a scriptural basis for law without treating a Wikipedia description of theocracy as evidence.

limit-guns.rationale: In the Crowder interview he explicitly opposes gun control, supports the Second Amendment and concealed carry, and offers no restrictive policy, while expressing discomfort with widespread open carry. This supplies a mature position absent from the earlier historical anecdote.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: To Crowder he says markets have failed to allocate resources efficiently for long-term industrial needs, and calls for public intervention.

more-religion-public.rationale: In the Carlson interview he insists that the political movement and country must be Christian; the Neel interview adds a Christian qualification for elected office.

nation-first.rationale: Calls himself an American nationalist and says "America First" is his immovable standard, including in foreign policy and trade.

natural-rulers.rationale: Told Carlson and Piers Morgan that men should lead and hold authority and that women should have no authority over men.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Wants the state to jail porn operators, deport immigrants and enforce Christian morals, and calls for reindustrialization.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Told Carlson that no-fault divorce laws let women leave marriages and collect child support and half the property without accountability, listing them among the problems.

open-borders.rationale: Calls for closing the border and mass deportation, and describes mass migration as the cause of civilizational loss.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Calls conservative and Republican leaders hypocrites and grifters and urged "drain the swamp", getting money and special interests out of politics.

premarital-sex.rationale: Told Piers Morgan sex is licit only within marriage as a Catholic, and criticised promiscuous women to Carlson.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Says his reason for being a conservative is that "we're losing our civilization because of mass immigration" and that the demographics must be conserved; says Christianity and white heritage should be central to the country.

race-social-construct.rationale: In the Morgan interview he says race is real, more than skin deep, and calls himself a racial realist in opposition to a colourblind account.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Told Carlson America needs to be "pro-white, not to the exclusion of everybody else", with white people having a special heritage as Americans; told Piers Morgan "I like my own people" and that every group seeks its own.

racial-pride.rationale: Told Carlson white people have a special heritage as Americans and the country should be pro-white; told Piers Morgan "I like my own people".

reason-over-faith.rationale: Grounds his positions on faith: says his Christian faith is why he rejects blood guilt and calls the Bible inspired scripture in full.

reduce-immigration.rationale: In the Carlson interview he identifies mass immigration as the cause of civilizational loss and argues that national demographics must be conserved; this addresses migration generally, alongside his calls for deportations.

religion-illusion.rationale: Describes himself as a deeply Catholic believer who bases his positions on Christian faith.

religious-nation.rationale: To Neel he says America must remain Christian and proposes a Christian qualification for elected office; this directly links national membership in government to religion.

restrict-private-adult-pornography-acces.rationale: Told Carlson porn is a huge social problem, agreed a Christian government would arrest and jail the owners of porn and OnlyFans sites, and said broad support exists.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Neel interview proposes requiring elected officials to profess Christianity while expressly rejecting government by the church. This rejects religious neutrality in office-holding, without the former unsupported claim of Catholic theocracy.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Told Piers Morgan there are two biologically distinct genders with different biological roles.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Told Carlson the wife is subordinate and "the authority rests with the man" in marriage, with the final say; she gives advice.

state-directs-investment.rationale: To Crowder he calls for strategic industrial subsidies, tax incentives, national production targets and a major public works programme, praising the CHIPS Act and asking for more.

state-harmful.rationale: Says he has moved away from libertarianism; now wants the state to enforce deportation, restrict porn and enforce Christian morality.

strong-leader.rationale: In the Carlson interview he urges the president to overcome state officials by force.

traditional-family.rationale: Argues for marriage, male authority in the household, and that porn, feminism and no-fault divorce erode family life.

vote-at-sixteen.rationale: In the Neel interview he proposes raising the voting age to 25, explicitly excluding sixteen-year-olds.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Told Piers Morgan the Bible says women have no authority over men and cannot teach men, which is why there are no female priests, and said he agrees with Catholic doctrine here.

women-must-cover.rationale: In the Neel interview he explicitly calls requiring women to cover completely with a niqab inhumane and says those religious laws go too far.

women-suffrage.rationale: Asked by Piers Morgan whether women should have the right to vote: "I do not. No. Absolutely not." and agreed they should stay at home; said women should not have equal rights.

notes: Later pass, 2026-11-08: reviewed every existing answer and every current statement, including candidates, against the Carlson and Morgan interviews and additional Neel interview. Automatic captions have no speaker labels, so retained answers from them are at most medium confidence and restricted to clear question-and-answer context. Checked the local reference-book filenames (no own book found), MediaSum (zero matching transcripts) and Lex Fridman (zero episodes); the local parliamentary corpora do not cover this commentator. Searched thin economy, ecology, technology, world, government and means themes, including healthcare, wages, taxation, climate, nuclear power, trade and alliances. Fight/Fudgie episode downloads returned 403; no further access to those episode pages attempted, and GitHub search found the Alex Jones mirror rather than the requested America First episodes. Secondary reports and jokes without a verified original were not converted into positions. Scholarly abstract s6 supplies context only; its critical characterisations do not establish answers. The Crowder interview supplies direct industrial-policy and gun-control positions. A retrieved 2022 oil clip mixes claims about infinite oil with an assertion that he is a scientist; without a clear sincere position it was not used to manufacture ecology answers. Moral neutrality of technology was not treated as political neutrality. No own book was found in the local reference library. Original automatic captions for the Neel interview were retrieved and checked against the third-party transcript; the third-party transcript is not cited as evidence. Final cross-check: the January 2024 violent-loyalty excerpt includes an immediate parody disclaimer, so it is not treated as a sincere contrary position or an action; uncertainty about sincerity keeps the nonviolence answer low. Reported July 2023 holy-war remarks led to a preserved video page without a readable transcript and a YouTube search with no relevant original result; those secondhand descriptions were not substituted for an inspected original. Arrests for obstruction were not treated as a general policy of suppressing political opposition. Final result: 59 to 49 known answers, 56 existing records changed, 102 candidate entries added; uncertainty passes.
